account:
Today town business seems unusually concentrated on bread, grain, and preparations in the great hall. My morning grain inspection established that the mill stall held seventy-three hay bales at two emeralds each, but neither available uncommitted stock nor delivery terms were confirmed. The secretary has made no purchase. Her written report records freight's order of two hundred loaves from the baker, with twenty-four emeralds and seventy-two wheat already received and another five hundred twenty-eight wheat needed at the time of that report. At tea, neighbour said builder reported that two hundred fresh loaves were now ready. I have not personally checked those loaves or learned their intended recipient.

There is also a lighting inspection in the great hall at eighteen, which I authorized yesterday. Neighbour says the new lighting looks splendid and builder intends to escort me. This could simply be the scheduled improvement and inspection; the bread order might be connected to a gathering, but I have no confirmation of that connection. I should attend rather than assume anything secret is happening.

Several townsfolk have repeated a strange, vague report of a 'bridge or port change at bakery,' naming baker and sometimes neighbour. Neighbour explicitly could not substantiate it and attributed what she heard to Townsfolk thirteen. I have seen no actual bridge or port change, so this remains gossip, not evidence of a project.

Neighbour also told me innkeeper wanted to discuss an unresolved account and a spoiled batch. Just now I heard baker addressing innkeeper about a separate thirty-emerald repayment, asking who owed whom and saying it must not be mixed with the bread and grain account. That suggests several transactions are being confused or still need settling; it does not establish wrongdoing or even the direction of the debt. I have asked baker for the details and await an answer.

The secretary reported no council letters at our earlier appointment. I returned for the sixteen-thirty office appointment late and still need her updated report. My impression is that baker, freight, innkeeper, builder, and neighbour know pieces of substantial provisioning and hall activity that I have not yet assembled. It may all be ordinary commerce and preparation for the inspection or another gathering, but its purpose is not yet clear to me.
